title: Scared of Shots? A Favorite Tune Helps Mute the Pain - Nautilus
gist: Needle fear (trypanophobia) may affect up to one in four UK adults per a 2021 Psychological Medicine study, and the panic response can amplify the pain of injections. Sufferers often skip vaccinations and other medical care; the available excerpt does not detail the music intervention named in the title.

insights.claim: A 2021 study in Psychological Medicine reported that trypanophobia, the fear of needles, may afflict up to one in four adults in the United Kingdom.
insights.speaker: Kristen French
insights.so_what: A large addressable population for needle-free delivery and anxiety-reduction interventions in healthcare.
insights.quote: A 2021 study in Psychological Medicine reported that it may afflict up to one in four adults in the United Kingdom.

insights.claim: People who fear needles may panic during blood draws or IV insertion, tensing muscles and spiking heart rate in ways that can amplify the pain of the injection.
insights.speaker: Kristen French
insights.so_what: Suggests simple behavioural interventions that reduce anxiety could measurably cut perceived procedural pain.
insights.quote: they may panic, tensing up their muscles and spiking their heart rate, which can amplify the pain of the poke

insights.claim: Some people with needle fear suffer a sustained shock of pain and anxiety that persists after the needle has been removed.
insights.speaker: Kristen French
insights.so_what: The burden of needle fear extends beyond the moment of injection, affecting patient experience.
insights.quote: Some people even suffer a sustained shock of pain and anxiety after the needle has come and gone.

insights.claim: People who fear needles often skip vaccinations and other medical care, which can have serious consequences for their health.
insights.speaker: Kristen French
insights.so_what: Needle fear depresses vaccine uptake, relevant to public-health programmes and vaccine makers' realised demand.
insights.quote: People who fear needles often skip vaccinations and other medical care.
